lectures.title: Summits of 2025-26: BRICS, SCO, ASEAN, G7 and India-hosted summits

items: **Venue:** Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; host: India, under its BRICS Presidency.
**Theme:** “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
**Fourth presidency:** India assumed its fourth BRICS Presidency on 1 January 2026; previous Indian presidencies: 2012, 2016 and 2021.
**Size of the grouping:** 11 full members and 10 partner countries.
**Share of the world:** member countries account for approximately 49.5% of global population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of global trade.
**Summit engagements:** involved 32 delegations: 11 member states, 10 partner states, four regional organisations and seven international organisations.
Leaders unanimously adopted the **New Delhi BRICS Leaders' Declaration** on 12 September 2026; it covered cooperation and the interests of the Global South.
**Terrorism:** condemned the 22 April 2025 terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people were killed.
**UN reform:** China and Russia supported India's and Brazil's aspirations for a greater role in the United Nations, including the Security Council.
**BRICS Continuity and Implementation Mechanism:** proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to follow up decisions across successive presidencies.

items: Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan

**Agriculture:** BRICS Centres of Excellence on Agro-Ecology and Regenerative Agriculture; BRICS Network on Digital Agriculture.
**Health and skills:** BRICS Mission for Healthy Lifestyle; BRICS CONNECT for Skilling.
**Enterprise:** BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal; BRICS Incubator Network; BRICS Logistics Supply-Chain Cooperation Framework.
**BRICS Payment Task Force:** continued work on interoperability of payment and financial messaging systems.
**Trade:** BRICS supported an open, transparent, fair and rules-based multilateral trading system centred on the WTO.
**Local currencies:** it supported local currencies in cross-border trade, investment and financial transactions.
**Energy:** it recognised the continued role of fossil fuels while supporting renewable energy, nuclear energy, hydropower, hydrogen and other low-carbon technologies.
**Women:** it emphasised women-led development and women's participation in governance and economic development.
**17th BRICS Summit:** 6–7 July 2025; venue: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; host country: Brazil.
**16th BRICS Summit:** held in October 2024 at Kazan, Russia.
**18th BRICS Summit:** was scheduled to be held in India in 2026.
**Venue:** Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic; chair: President Sadyr Japarov.
**28 documents approved:** covering security, emergencies, climate, energy and institutional cooperation.
**New centres:** measures for a Universal Centre for Countering Challenges and Threats and an SCO Anti-Drug Centre were approved.
**RATS:** these centres would complement the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) in Tashkent.
**Attendance:** Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the summit.
**India's approach** centred on Security, Connectivity and Opportunity.
**Terrorism:** called for dismantling the terrorist ecosystem; opposed double standards in counter-terrorism.
**Diplomacy:** stressed dialogue and diplomacy; linked Eurasian security with peace in Afghanistan.
**Connectivity:** supported connectivity that promotes trade while respecting sovereignty and territorial integrity.
**Language:** supported English as an official SCO language alongside Russian and Chinese.
**SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum:** India announced that it would host the first forum later in 2026.
**Origin:** originated from the Shanghai Five of 1996; established: 15 June 2001.
**Full membership:** 10 countries. India and Pakistan joined in 2017; Iran in 2023; Belarus in 2024.
**Presidency:** Kyrgyzstan transferred the 2026–27 presidency to Pakistan.
**Theme:** “Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity.”
**Next summit:** Pakistan is scheduled to host the next summit in 2027.
**Lahore:** designated SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026–27.
**Venue:** Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu, Philippines; chair: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
**Focus:** the summit focused on ASEAN's future and regional cooperation.
**ASEAN cooperation areas** included Political-Security, Economic and Socio-Cultural.
**ASEAN–India Plan of Action 2026–2030:** adopted in Kuala Lumpur.
**ASEAN–India Year of Maritime Cooperation:** 2026 designated for maritime cooperation.
**23rd ASEAN–India Summit:** was expected to follow in 2026.
